method: Each retained link was checked against two opened sources. Notes are paraphrases, not quotations. Dates for people are lifespans; a single year means birth. Dates for bands begin with formation. Place is birthplace or formation city.

sources.title: Kommersant Weekend: 10 albums of September
sources.evidence: The Aquarium subsection explicitly identifies Vavilon as originally written as reggae. Full body retrieved with urllib.

sources.title: Colta: Interview with Levsha Patsan about Aquarium in Dub
sources.evidence: The producer discusses Vavilon as an early Soviet reggae song and identifies its roots-reggae style.

sources.title: Muzykalnaya Pravda: Lagutenko’s Prekrasny diletant
sources.evidence: December 2012 report names the cover and includes Lagutenko explaining his interpretation. Opened via Python urllib after web timeouts.

sources.title: Afisha Volna: Nick Cave, The Killers, R.E.M., Mumiy Troll and others
sources.evidence: December 4, 2012 roundup identifies Mumiy Troll’s recording as the final cover in the Aquarium tribute.

sources.title: Colta: Andrey Makarevich interview, June 2019
sources.evidence: At the start of the interview Makarevich explicitly confirms the Beatles as a songwriting influence.

sources.title: Radio Liberty: Andrey Makarevich interview, December 2003
sources.evidence: Near the end, asked about Beatles influence on his band, Makarevich acknowledges their profound impression.

sources.title: Smithsonian Folkways: Big Mama Thornton, Ball N’ Chain liner notes
sources.evidence: Chris Strachwitz’s liner notes, PDF page 3, identify Thornton’s composition and Joplin’s recording.

sources.title: The Guardian: Big Mama Thornton profile
sources.evidence: Confirms the cover.

sources.title: Eric Clapton: Official biography
sources.evidence: The paragraph following Reptile describes the Robert Johnson covers assembled into the March 2004 album.

sources.title: All About Jazz: Me and Mr. Johnson review
sources.evidence: Doug Collette reviews the Robert Johnson tribute and lists all fourteen songs with Johnson credits.

sources.title: musicOMH: Joss Stone — The Soul Sessions
sources.evidence: John Murphy’s 2003 review explicitly describes the White Stripes cover and changed title.

sources.title: Apple Music: The Soul Sessions editorial album note
sources.evidence: Editorial note identifies the White Stripes original and Stone’s remake; linked music video bears the Boy title.

sources.title: Concord: Creedence Clearwater Revival, 40th Anniversary Edition
sources.evidence: Record label identifies the Screamin’ Jay Hawkins cover on the debut album.

sources.title: El País: El salvaje más truculento
sources.evidence: Diego A. Manrique identifies Creedence among the artists who recorded Hawkins’s song.

sources.title: MOJO: Deep Purple Made in Japan reviewed
sources.evidence: James McNair identifies Lucille as Little Richard’s song in the 1972 Japan recordings; expanded tracklist dates it to Osaka, August 16.

sources.title: metal.de: Deep Purple — In Concert ’72 reissue review
sources.evidence: Markus Endres identifies the Little Richard cover in the BBC concert recorded in London on March 9, 1972. Independent performance corroborates the shared cover claim.

sources.title: Mississippi Blues Trail: Big Joe Williams
sources.evidence: Historical marker text lists Van Morrison with Them among artists who covered Williams’s signature song.

sources.title: Connswater Community Greenway: Mystic of the East — The Van Morrison Trail
sources.evidence: Printed page 7 (PDF page 4) identifies Them’s recording as a Big Joe Williams cover. Independent Belfast heritage guide hosted by the artist.

sources.title: NPR Morning Edition: Singer Joe Cocker dies at 70 (BPR transcript)
sources.evidence: Archival Cocker interview explains how he changed the rhythm of the Ray Charles number.

sources.title: Contemporary Musicians: Joe Cocker (Encyclopedia.com)
sources.evidence: Joan Goldsworthy and Bruce Walker describe the title cover and album tribute to Charles. Avoided conflicting discography date; no date claimed.
